subject: mouse
title: Mice Pull Out Their Unconscious Friends' Tongues to Revive Them

scenes.text: Mice pull out each other's tongues. It's a rescue.
Scientists put one mouse to sleep with anesthesia, then watched its cage mate.
The friend sniffed it, groomed it, bit at its mouth, and pulled its tongue out. Over half of them did it.
Why? It clears the airway. When researchers put an object in the sleeping mouse's mouth, rescuers removed it eight times in ten.
Mice that got the treatment woke up faster.
And they tried hardest for mice they knew. First aid, no training.

description:
In a 2025 Science study, mice spent about half of a 13-minute test tending an anesthetized cage mate: sniffing, grooming, biting at its mouth and pulling its tongue.
Pulling the tongue opened the airway and removed objects placed in the mouth most of the time, and treated mice recovered sooner. The behaviour was strongest between familiar mice.
Have you seen a pet do something like this?
first_comment: The behaviour did not fade when the test was repeated over five days; it slightly increased. Do you think animals feel empathy?
